one should associate with the supreme person;”
One should abide by his instruction,
like one who has climbed onto a small piece of wood.
Just as one might sink in the great ocean,
so too does even a person of virtuous life sink by associating with the indolent.
Therefore, one should avoid that person who is indolent and lacking in energy;
[one should associate] with the noble ones who dwell in seclusion.
One should dwell together with wise people who are self-controlled, meditative, and always possessed of aroused energy.
… The Elder Vimala … The Third Chapter is finished.
Sobhita, Vāraṇa, and the seer Isidatta;
